conf.description: zos-racf racinit / other: hand-built IRRADU00 unload parse for SMF80 event01 (RACINIT logon), site formatter output assumed KVP using the literal INIT_ column names per this technology family's established precedent (zos-smf, zos-acf2); event.outcome/source.address/racf.auth_reason/timestamp computed before the batched rename.

conf.comment: zos-racf / racinit / other. No Elastic integration or Cribl pack exists for RACF/IRRADU00. The work order gives the IRRADU00 header/extension byte-offset boundaries (1-280, 282+) but not the per-column byte widths for most INIT_ fields, so a true fixed-position slice cannot be built without inventing widths for ~15 undocumented columns. Following this corpus's precedent for the same ambiguity (zos-smf tcpip/dataset-access), the site formatter/unload-to-text step is assumed to emit self-describing KEY=VALUE tokens using the literal INIT_ names the field table gives, extracted via serde kvp. NOT confirmed against a real unload sample - flagged in the README. EVENT_TYPE and EVENT_QUAL/VIOLATION/SMFID/USER_NAME/LOGSTR widths ARE stated or platform-conventional, but that only matters for a true byte-offset build, which this is not. Direct route, no guard hop; LPAR UTC offset is not given anywhere in the work order, so _time uses a naive Date.parse with no zone correction (documented gap).
